title: Lensway canvas: orchestration matrix for console navigation, dashboards, and rollout lenses
creator: Maya Chen
description: High-level redesign that reframes the Redwood Console as a lens-based canvas: users compose contextual 'lenses' (Dashboard Lens, Rollout Lens, Cost Lens, Debug Lens) rather than navigating deep, rigid rails. The Lensway Canvas bundles workspace switching, route-aware context, and model/route-specific controls into lightweight micro-surfaces. This ticket captures prototypes, design reviews, trade-offs, and the initial handoff package for engineering to implement an incremental rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype validated in two usability sessions with PM and SRE participants showing <=2 extra clicks for switching primary workspace context
Figma prototype includes: collapsed Lens strip, active-lens breadcrumbs, workspace chip behavior, and cost breakdown micro-interaction states
Design tokens and spacing rules provided; accessible contrast and keyboard flows documented
Handoff includes annotated component variants and an engineer FAQ covering routing fallback behavior and telemetry events
engineering_dependencies: ENG-23145 (route-aware breadcrumb service): must land API for active-lens -> route mapping
ENG-23792 (workspace switch API v2): atomic switch with optimistic UI and telemetry
ENG-24001 (cost micro-metrics): event surface for per-route token/cost attribution
decisions: Adopt 'lenses' as the primary conceptual model. Each lens is a modular surface that can be pinned to the canvas or floated as a quick overlay.
Left navigation becomes a slim Lens strip (icons + micro-labels). Expanded details live in the canvas header rather than a deep panel.
Workspace switching surfaces as a compact 'workspace chip' in the global header — clicking opens an inline panel rather than a full modal to preserve context.
Rollout controls (canary / A/B / fallback) surface as a lens-level toolbar so engineers can perform quick rollouts without leaving the dashboard.
Cost view integrates token and inference unit slides in a collapsible micro-card attached to the Dashboard Lens; default collapsed to reduce noise.
Routing fallback: when a pinned model variant is unavailable, the Lensway router will surface a lightweight inline chooser rather than a full nav redirect.
notes: Usability sessions (1/28, 2/03): PMs liked inline workspace chip; SREs requested clearer failure states for routing fallback
Accessibility review (2/05): keyboard focus order updated for lens strip; added aria-live region for rollout state changes
Performance concern: initial canvas render shows +140ms for telemetry binding in large orgs — engineering follow-up required
Design trade-off: we intentionally deprioritized a full left rail expansion to keep the canvas visually lightweight; may revisit for power users
feedback_from_pm: Keep cost micro-cards dismissible; we want ops to surface them only when investigating regressions
Expose an 'audit snapshot' button in the Rollout Lens to capture current rollout config for incident triage
Ensure that workspace chip preserves last-used lens when switching back and forth
feedback_from_engineering: Prefer declarative telemetry events rather than ad-hoc calls from UI; see ENG-23145 for the required contract
Suggest implementing the collapsed Lens strip as a CSS-driven variant with minimal JS to reduce bundle size
Routing fallback chooser should accept a list of compatible quantized variants — backend will provide mapping via route metadata
prototype_findings: Participants found the 'float-to-pin' gesture for lenses intuitive after a short onboarding hint
Two participants attempted to find rollout history under project settings; added a small history icon in the Rollout Lens header
Cost micro-card default collapsed reduced perceived clutter; however, heavy-cost customers asked for a persistent 'cost monitor' pin option
